judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseResult wrapper ({success, data}), but this call site stores that wrapper as the entire credential key, whereas the replaced googleCredentialSchema.parse(...) returned the parsed credentials object directly. After the first token refresh (in both sync and non-sync modes), credential.key becomes {success:true,data:{...}} instead of the credentials object; every reader of credential.key.access_token / .expiry_date gets undefined, so Google Calendar operations fail for the affected user until the row is manually repaired.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (a `SafeParseResult` with `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed `data` itself. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credentials are persisted as `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); ... prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, which will store the wrapper object as the credential `key` rather than the credentials payload. Previously it stored the parsed object via `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`. This mismatch is diff-verifiable and would break later reads expecting `credential.key.access_token` etc.
